source.page_label: Lab Exercise # 5: Analyzing Complex DC Circuits using Nodal and Mesh Analysis

statement: Consider the complex DC circuit in Fig 1. The DC voltage source setting is 8 V (i.e. Vs = 8 V), and the resistor values are: R1 = 1 kΩ, R2 = 2.2 kΩ, R3 = 820 Ω, R4 = 220 Ω, R5 = 470 Ω, and R6 = 330 Ω. Use nodal analysis to compute the nodal voltages of this circuit. Show your “complete step-by-step” work including equations and calculations within the space provided in the Prelab-5 Worksheet and record your answers in Table 1 of the worksheet.

source.page_label: Lab Exercise # 8: The Oscilloscope and the Function Generator

statement: Task 1. Theoretical Calculations: For each circuit, given in Figures 1 – 3 (shown below), the AC source signal, Vs, is given by: Vs(t) = 5 sin(12566.4t) V. The circuit component values are given as follows: R1 = 2.2 kΩ, R2 = 820 Ω, C = 82 nF, L = 68 mH. a. Calculate the frequency, period, amplitude, peak-to-peak and rms values of the source signal. Show “complete step-by-step” work including equations and calculations within the given space in the Prelab-8 Worksheet.

Task 1. Theoretical Calculations: a. For the circuit in Fig. 1, perform analytical calculations to determine the value of RL. The power supplied by the 12V source should be 87.11 mW and the power supplied by the 5V source should be 3.44 mW. b. Use the Superposition Theorem to determine – (i) the current through RL only due to the 12V source, (ii) the current in RL only due to the 5V source, and (iii) the current through RL with both voltage sources connected to the circuit. Note: When computing the current through RL only due to the 12V source, you need to replace the 5V source with a short-circuit. Consequently, to compute the current through RL only due to the 5V source, you need to replace the 12V source with a short-circuit. c. Complete row 1 of Table 1 in the Prelab-7 Worksheet.
